name: Boiled Currant Pudding
description: Historical recipe from The Whitehouse Cookbook (1887). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: one-half a cupful of chopped suet
ingredients.originalText: one-half a cupful of chopped suet

instructions.text: Sift two teaspoonfuls of baking powder into five cupfuls of sifted flour
Wash the currants, dry them thoroughly and pick away any stalks or grit
Mix all the ingredients together and moisten with sufficient milk to make the pudding into a stiff batter
Tie it up in a floured cloth and put it into boiling water
Boil for three hours and a half
Serve with jelly sauce made very sweet

source.author: F.L. Gillette
source.originalInstructions:
1. Sift two teaspoonfuls of baking powder into five cupfuls of sifted flour
2. Wash the currants, dry them thoroughly and pick away any stalks or grit
3. Chop the suet finely
4. Mix all the ingredients together and moisten with sufficient milk to make the pudding into a stiff batter
5. Tie it up in a floured cloth and put it into boiling water
6. Boil for three hours and a half
7. Serve with jelly sauce made very sweet
